introHeroTitle: Explore Canada's ocean data on one map
introHeroText: Find measurements of the ocean around Canada, like temperature, salinity, currents and marine life. Scientists, governments and communities collected them. Everything is free to explore and download.
introShowcase_trajectory_body: See the route an underwater glider took off Vancouver Island.
introShowcase_stations_title: Zoom into the Gulf of St. Lawrence
introShowcase_stations_body: Get close enough to see each place where data was collected.
introShowcase_coverage_body: See how much data was collected over time.
introShowcase_nonna_title: See the seafloor in Halifax Harbour
introShowcase_nonna_body: Show how deep the water is, measured by the Canadian Hydrographic Service.
introFeature_explore_body: Darker colours mean more data. Click anywhere to see what was measured there.
introFeature_search_body: Search by keyword, or filter by what was measured, when and where.
introFeature_download_body: Download it, or open it where it's published.
introTipsText: Short tips pop up on the map while you explore. When one is waiting, look for the <icon/> button.
tipInfoFeedback: Something not working, or have an idea? We read every message.
introReopenText: Open this window again with the <icon/> button beside the Data Explorer title.
introSources: Data comes from ERDDAP™ servers run by CIOOS and its partners, and from OBIS, the Ocean Biodiversity Information System.
tipsToggleLabel: Show tips on the map as I use the Explorer
tip_whatsHere: <add/> adds a dataset to your selection. It stays as you pan and filter, so you can gather datasets from several clicks before downloading.
tip_inView: Only want what's on screen? The In view button beside the dataset count keeps just the datasets in the map view.
tip_timeCoverage: Not sure which dates to pick? Time coverage in the top bar charts the data over time.
tip_speciesName: Looking for a species? In Filters, Scientific Name also finds common names, like “killer whale”.
tip_exclude: Filters can leave things out too: <exclude/> at the end of an option's row excludes it, like a platform type or a data portal you don't want.
tip_matchAll: Picked several ocean variables? Turn on “Match all included options” to keep only the datasets that measure every one.
tip_realtime: Want live data? The Real-time button beside the dataset count keeps only datasets still sending data at the last harvest.
tip_showData: Show data plots a feature's measurements, or lists them in a table, so you can check them before downloading.
tip_trajectory: In the legend's Trajectories group, step the date to see where each platform was that day. The menu beside Track sets how much of its path is drawn behind it.
tip_griddapWms: Turn on Show on map to draw a gridded dataset, then pick a variable and step through time and depth.
tip_filtersCutDownload: Your time, depth and area filters also cut the download: narrow them to get smaller files with only the data you need.
tip_directLinks: No email needed: Direct links in the Download window fetch each dataset straight from its server, with no 1 GB limit, or save them as a curl script.
tip_shareLink: The page address saves your view, filters, area and open dataset. Copy it to share, or bookmark it.
submissionStateTextSuccess: Request received. A download link will be emailed to {{email}} when your files are ready. Check your spam folder if it doesn't arrive.
submissionStateTextFailedNetwork: Couldn't reach the server. Check your connection, then resubmit.
submissionStateTextFailedRejected: The server refused this request. Try narrowing your filters or selection, then resubmit.
submissionStateTextFailedServer: The server ran into a problem. Please try again in a few minutes.
downloadModalSubtitleText: Review your selection, then receive it as a prepared archive by email or download it directly from the source.
downloadRememberEmailLabel: Remember my email on this device
downloadEmailNotice: We use your email only to send you this download, and delete it 7 days after the download is processed, keeping just its domain (such as uvic.ca) for usage statistics.
privacyModalSubtitle: What this site keeps, what leaves your browser, and why.
privacy_device_title: Saved in your browser, not by us
privacy_device_body: This site sets no cookies. Your browser keeps a few settings for it on this device: your language, map layers and projection, which tips you've seen, whether you've closed the About window, and your email address if you ask it to be remembered. They are never sent to us. Clearing this site's data in your browser erases them.
privacy_email_body: Used only to send you the download link, or to tell you it failed. The message goes out through Google's Gmail service (<google>Google's privacy policy</google>). We delete the address from our download records 7 days after your download is processed. Only its domain (the part after the @, such as uvic.ca) is kept, to count downloads by institution.
privacy_errors_body: When something breaks, a report of what failed and on which page goes to Sentry, a service based in the United States (<sentry>Sentry's privacy policy</sentry>). It does not include your IP address or your email address. Feedback you send with the feedback button goes there too, with your email address only if you choose to give it.
privacy_analytics_body: We count visits with Plausible, run by CIOOS. It uses no cookies and keeps no personal information, only totals such as pages viewed, which site you came from, and how many download requests are submitted (with the number of datasets and the language, never your email address).
privacy_map_body: Your browser loads map backgrounds directly from their providers (EMODnet, OpenFreeMap and, for satellite imagery, Esri). Like any website, they see your IP address and which part of the map you are viewing.
privacy_rights_body: To ask what we hold about you, or to have it corrected or deleted, see the <guidelines>CIOOS privacy guidelines</guidelines>.

oceanVariableFilterTooltip: Filter data by ocean variable name. Selection works as logical OR operation; switch on "Match all selected variables" to keep only data measuring every one of them.
platformFilterTooltip: Filter data by platform type. Click an option to include it, or the exclude button at the end of its row to exclude it; click again to undo. Included options work as logical OR; excluded ones are removed from the result.
organizationFilterTooltip: Filter data by responsible organisation name. Click an option to include it, or the exclude button at the end of its row to exclude it; click again to undo. Included options work as logical OR; excluded ones are removed from the result.

datasetFilterTooltip: Filter data by dataset name. Click an option to include it, or the exclude button at the end of its row to exclude it; click again to undo. Included options work as logical OR; excluded ones are removed from the result.
sourceFilterTooltip: Filter data by data portal: ERDDAP servers and OBIS nodes. Clicking ERDDAP or OBIS includes or excludes all of its sources; collapse or expand it with its arrow. Click an option to include it, or the exclude button at the end of its row to exclude it; click again to undo. Included options work as logical OR; excluded ones are removed from the result.

scientificNameFilterTooltip: Filter OBIS data by scientific or common name. Common-name matches (e.g. "killer whale") resolve to the underlying scientific name via the World Register of Marine Species. Selection works as logical OR. Downloaded records still contain all species in the matching datasets.

coverageOrganizationNote: A dataset can belong to several organizations, so it is counted under each one. The stacked bars can therefore total more than the number of datasets.

coverageViewHelp_seasonal: Every year stacked onto one January-to-December axis, by week, to show when in the year the data was collected.
coverageSeasonalNote: All years in the time window are added together, week by week. The last week runs from December 24 to 31.

selectionHelp_add_body: Click the + beside a dataset's title in the list. You can also add one straight from the map: click a point or a cell and use “Add this dataset to the selection” on the card that opens. Either way the count at the bottom of the list goes up.
selectionHelp_remove_title: Remove one, or change your mind later
selectionHelp_remove_body: A selected dataset shows a filled tick instead of the +. Click it again to take it out. The selection survives panning, filtering and searching, so you can gather datasets across several map clicks, and the Download window lets you untick anything before you submit.
selectionHelp_grid_body: Gridded (griddap) datasets are catalogued here but not served by the CDE, so their selection control is disabled. Open the dataset to reach its ERDDAP™ server and take the data there, where you can subset it yourself.
selectionHelp_size_body: In the Download window every selected dataset is measured against your filters. Anything still larger than 1 GB can't be delivered as a prepared archive: it is unticked and marked with a red cross, and the direct source link listed beside the order is how you get it. Narrowing the time, depth or map area usually brings it back under the limit.
selectionHelp_filters_title: Your filters travel with the order
selectionHelp_filters_body: Time, depth and the drawn area are applied to the download, and each can be switched off in the Download window. Three exceptions: direct ERDDAP™ links use the bounding box of a drawn polygon rather than its exact shape, datasets with no depth variable ignore the depth filter, and OBIS records come as the full dataset snapshot.
sidebarShowMapTitle: Show the map — the dataset stays open in a card
apiErrorBannerText: The data service is not responding, so filters and datasets could not be loaded.
apiErrorPointsBannerText: The data service is not responding, so the dataset list could not be loaded.

harvest.downloads.queueStalled_other: {{count}} download requests are queued with nothing processing them. The download scheduler may not be running.

harvest.downloads.noDatasetDetail: No per-dataset detail was recorded for this request.

harvest.downloads.reason.partial: Only part of this dataset was included.
realtimeFilterTooltip: Show only datasets that were still producing data when they were last harvested.
realtimeFilterHelpText: Datasets whose newest data was less than a week old when we last checked.
datasetRealtimeBadgeTitle: This dataset was still producing data when it was last harvested. Coverage is across all of its records, as reported by the server.
directLinksTooltipText: Fetch each dataset straight from the server that publishes it, with no email, no queue and no 1 GB ceiling. The links carry whichever filters are switched on above. ERDDAP links use the bounding box of a drawn polygon; OBIS links use the polygon itself. Each export also carries the dataset's CIOOS catalogue record (licence, citation, contacts).
directLinksNotePolygon: ERDDAP links constrain by the latitude/longitude box around your selection. Where that selection is a drawn polygon rather than a rectangle, the files will include data from outside the shape.
directLinksNoteDepth_one: {{count}} dataset has no depth variable; its link leaves the depth filter out.
directLinksNoteDepth_other: {{count}} datasets have no depth variable; their links leave the depth filter out.
directLinksNoteUnfiltered_one: {{count}} OBIS snapshot is the whole dataset, unfiltered.
directLinksNoteUnfiltered_other: {{count}} OBIS snapshots are whole datasets, unfiltered.
legendHelp_observations_body: Hexagon colour and marker size count the same thing: days of data, meaning the distinct days on which anything was measured in that place.
legendHelp_hexes_body: Zoomed out, every dataset in view is summed into hexagonal cells, whatever kind of data it holds.
legendHelp_markers_body: Zoomed in past level 7, profile and time-series datasets stop being cells and are drawn at the locations they were collected from.
legendHelp_trajectories_line_body: The path a moving platform followed. Tracks ignore the time filter and draw the trailing window below instead.
legendHelp_trajectories_trail_body: How much history is drawn before the selected date. Zoomed out, the long windows load at most one year.
legendHelp_trajectories_head_body: Where the platform was on the selected date, and which way it was going. Set the date with the rail underneath.
legendHelp_seafloor_source_body: CHS NONNA soundings, drawn as part of the basemap. The ramp appears once the map is zoomed in far enough for those soundings to be drawn.
legendHelp_seafloor_reading_body: CHS publishes these tiles as colour rather than depth values, so the scale was calibrated from the imagery. Read it as bands, not contours; the bar is logarithmic.
legendHelp_layers_griddap_body: The bounding box of each gridded (griddap) dataset matching your filters. Gridded data is continuous over its whole box, so there is nothing to count per cell. It is drawn as an outline, not a colour ramp.
legendHelp_layers_download_body: The CDE does not prepare downloads for gridded data. Open a dataset to reach its ERDDAP™ server.
legendHelp_observations_once_body: However many datasets sampled it. Two moorings and a glider all recording on 1 January are one day of data between them, not three.
legendHelp_observations_gaps_body: The count follows the real sampling calendar: a station visited every January contributes those days alone, not the years in between.
legendHelp_observations_why_body: Record counts mix three different units across our sources (measurements, occurrence records and position fixes), and some are estimated from a sampling rate rather than measured. A day means the same thing everywhere, so any two places can be compared.
legendHelp_markers_size_body: Marker size shows the same count as a hexagon's colour. A marker is at its smallest at or below the number shown beside the small circle and grows from there. Where every location holds the same count there is no ramp to show, so they are all drawn at one size.
legendHelp_markers_colour_body: Mooring, ship, glider, and so on. Only the platform types present in your current results are listed, so the key never promises a colour the map is not drawing.
legendHelp_markers_cells_body: Trajectory tracks and OBIS occurrences are swept into coverage hexagons at every zoom, so those hexagons stay on the map underneath the markers.
legendHelp_hexes_hover_body: A cell's colour is a total. Point at one and its tooltip names what that total is made of.
legendHelp_hexes_scale_title: Scaled to what is on screen
legendHelp_hexes_scale_body: The scale is recalculated for the hexagons in view, so the same green means different amounts at different zooms.
